  - paragraph: Make a short Fact or Fiction journey for someone curious or sceptical about Jesus. Help them think about whether the story of Jesus can be trusted, give them a little historical context, and finish by asking who they think Jesus was. Use the matching NUA video as part of it. Keep it welcoming and let them express what they actually think.
  - paragraph: That sounds like a great starting point. I'll build a short, welcoming Fact or Fiction journey using the approved video, some historical context, and a final question on who they think Jesus was.
  - text: Plan
  - paragraph: "Fact or Fiction: Can We Trust Jesus? 1. welcome: Welcome the visitor warmly and set up the question of whether Jesus' story can be trusted. 2. video: Play the intro to the 'Fact or Fiction' video to start the discussion on historical trust. 3. reflection: Offer a short reflection on why the reliability of the story matters for trust. 4. evidence: Ask the visitor what they think about the evidence presented in the video. 5. who-was-jesus: Close by asking a personal question about who the visitor believes Jesus was. Assumed: Used the 'fact-or-fiction' library video for the video step, specifically the introduction section (0-133 seconds) to keep the journey short and focused on the core question. Assumed: Chose a poll for the 'evidence' step to provide a quick, structured way for the user to express their initial reaction before the free-form closing question. Assumed: Chose a textResponse for the final step to allow the user to express exactly what they think in their own words, fulfilling the brief's request to 'let them express what they actually think'. Assumed: Used a 'background image' for the welcome and reflection cards to provide visual appeal without cluttering the short text content."
  - paragraph: Here's the plan. Shall I build it?
  - paragraph: Yes, build it.
  - paragraph: The opening card's button is too low. Make the opening copy shorter so the button is comfortably above the footer without scrolling, and use a short muted background clip from the same film behind it. Keep the other cards as they are.
  - paragraph: I'll shorten the welcome copy and swap the background image for a muted clip from the 'Fact or Fiction' video so the button sits comfortably above the footer.
  - paragraph: Use dark mode on every card. Set both the welcome background video and the main video to Fit so the whole video is visible at its original aspect ratio, with no zoom or edge cropping. Keep the wording, clip timings and navigation unchanged.
  - paragraph: I’ll set every card to dark mode and switch the welcome background video and the main video to “Fit” so the full frame is visible without cropping, keeping all text, timings, and navigation exactly as they are.
  - text: Plan
  - paragraph: "- update welcome-card: Set the card theme to dark. - update welcome-card: Add objectFit \"fit\" to the backgroundVideo so the muted clip shows the whole frame at its original aspect ratio. - update reflection-card: Set the card theme to dark. - update who-was-jesus-card: Set the card theme to dark. - update video-player: Add objectFit \"fit\" to the standalone video so it displays the whole frame with no zoom or cropping. Assumed: The 'video' and 'evidence' steps already use the default dark theme, so no explicit change is needed for them. Assumed: No wording, startAt/endAt timings, or navigation links are changed, per the brief."
  - paragraph: Here's the plan. Shall I build it?
  - paragraph: Yes, apply these changes.
  - paragraph: Cards 3 and 5 are still light. Change the reflection and who-was-jesus steps to dark mode, with light text on a dark background. Keep all wording, video settings and navigation as they are.
  - paragraph: I'll switch the 'reflection' and 'who-was-jesus' cards to dark mode to ensure the text is light and the background is dark, keeping all other content exactly as is.
  - paragraph: Make a side-by-side-in-sequence comparison using three consecutive video cards. Keep the existing main video card as Fit, then add a Fill video card and a Crop video card immediately after it. All three must use the exact same Fact or Fiction library video and the same 0–133 second clip, in dark mode. Use the native Fit, Fill and Crop options, not different video clips. After Crop, continue to the existing reflection card. Keep the welcome background video, all existing text and all response cards unchanged.
  - paragraph: I'll add two new video cards after the existing main video — one set to Fill and one to Crop — all using the same 0–133 s 'Fact or Fiction' clip in dark mode, then continue to the reflection card.
  - text: Plan
  - paragraph: "- update video: Re-point next to 'video-fill' so the sequence flows into the new comparison cards. - add video-fill: Insert a new step after 'video' with a standalone dark-mode card containing the 'fact-or-fiction' library video (0–133 s) using objectFit 'fill'. - add video-crop: Insert a new step after 'video-fill' with a standalone dark-mode card containing the 'fact-or-fiction' library video (0–133 s) using objectFit 'zoomed' (Crop). Its next points to 'reflection'. Assumed: The 'video' step's card already has theme dark and objectFit 'fit' as established in prior turns, so no content change is needed there beyond the next pointer. Assumed: The new 'video-fill' and 'video-crop' steps use dark theme to match the brief's requirement for dark mode on all three comparison cards. Assumed: All existing text, navigation, and response cards (welcome, reflection, evidence, who-was-jesus) remain unchanged per the brief."
